samples.summary: Copy grants the copier document-manager rights over a byte-identical duplicate, escalating a plain member past the editor-share-link and move gates
samples.evidence: The copy endpoint is deliberately gated on workspace membership only (document.controller.ts:296-307), and DocumentCopyService sets `author: { connect: { id: userId } }` (document-copy.service.ts:81). `isDocumentManager` treats the author as a manager, so the copier becomes a manager of content they were explicitly NOT a manager of. Concretely: (a) share-link.service.ts:86 denies a non-manager the ability to mint an *editor* (anonymous write) share link — the comment at share-link.service.ts:127-131 calls that escalation out by name — but the same user can POST /documents/:id/copy and then mint an editor link on the identical content; (b) document.controller.ts:230-285 / :332-347 restrict moving a document to managers, yet the copier can move the copy into any other workspace they belong to, carrying the source's full content across a workspace boundary in two requests. The design doc's risk table (docs/design/document-copy.md, "A reader copies a document to escape a permission boundary → There is no boundary to escape") only considers the copy's initial location and misses the authorship grant. Mitigating: a member already has rw on the source and could export/re-upload manually, so this lowers the bar rather than creating access from nothing.

samples.summary: New S3 sink `FileService.copy(source.fileId)` skips the `VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN` check every other blob path applies, and launders an arbitrary storage key into a servable UUID id
samples.evidence: Every other place a DB-sourced `fileId` reaches S3 validates it first: document-file.controller.ts:51, api/v1/files.controller.ts:140, document.controller.ts:387 and :428, api/v1/documents.controller.ts:128. document-copy.service.ts:63-64 passes `source.fileId` straight into `FileService.copy`, which interpolates it into `CopySource` (file.service.ts:145) with no pattern check. The laundering is what makes this dangerous: the *destination* id is a fresh `randomUUID()+ext` (file.service.ts:140), which passes `VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN`, so any object the CopyObject can reach becomes downloadable through the validated GET path on a document the attacker owns — turning a non-servable/foreign key into a servable one. I could not find a writer that admits an unvalidated fileId today (document.dto.ts:38 and :69 apply `@Matches(VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN)`, api/v1/files.controller.ts:114 uses the id returned by upload), so this is currently defense-in-depth rather than a live exploit — hence low confidence, but major impact if any writer (script, import path, future endpoint) ever relaxes.

samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copies sheet comment threads, contradicting the documented "comments are deliberately not carried over" boundary
samples.evidence: copyContent's JSON-root arm assigns every root key onto the target (document-copy.service.ts:188-198) for `sheet`/`slides`/`board`. Sheet worksheets store comment threads inside that root (`comments?: { [threadId: string]: Thread }`, packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94 and the seeded `comments: {}` at :147), so discussion threads — including their author identities and @mention data — are duplicated into the new document. Both docs/design/document-copy.md ("Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over") and the service's own class comment (document-copy.service.ts:35-37) assert the opposite. Impact is bounded because the copier can already read those comments in the source, but combined with the copier becoming manager of the copy it moves other users' comment content into a document the copier can expose via a share link.

samples.summary: Authenticated storage/cost amplification: one small copy request duplicates up to 50 MB in object storage with no quota
samples.evidence: POST /documents/:id/copy sits under the default 120 req/min throttle (app.module.ts:98) and each request triggers a full-size server-side CopyObject (file.service.ts:138-148) plus, for JSON-root types, a whole document root parsed into backend memory (document-copy.service.ts:179-187, snapshotJsonRoot at :212). No per-user/per-workspace storage or document quota exists anywhere in the backend (grep for quota/storageLimit/maxDocuments returns nothing), so a single authenticated member can grow bucket usage by ~6 GB/min from a source blob they already uploaded. Comparable amplification already exists on upload, so this is an extension of an existing gap rather than a new class of problem.

samples.summary: Unbounded re-parse loop in `snapshotJsonRoot` over document-controlled data
samples.evidence: `while (typeof value === 'string') { value = JSON.parse(value); }` (document-copy.service.ts:213-215) iterates without a depth cap on data derived from a collaboratively-editable document root. I could not construct a Yorkie root whose `toJSON()` yields a string that re-parses to another string (the root always serializes as an object), so I could not complete an exploit chain; a fixed unwrap depth would remove the question entirely.

verdict.reason: The cited lines are present (copy is membership-gated at document.controller.ts:296-307; document-copy.service.ts:81 sets author=userId; isDocumentManager treats author as manager at document-access.ts:21; editor-link gate at share-link.service.ts:86-90), but the claimed escalation is not one. Counterexample: a plain member can already reach the identical end state without the copy endpoint. (a) Membership alone grants rw on every document's CRDT content — YorkieAuthController.hasAccess, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:176-189 ("Membership grants read+write; the model has no per-member viewer role today") — and blob bytes are member-readable at document-file.controller.ts:79-85. (b) Any member can create a document authored by themselves, in any workspace they belong to, via assertMember-only endpoints that set author: { connect: { id: userId } } (document.controller.ts:203-224 and :124-142); being the author makes them a manager by document-access.ts:21. (c) Blobs can be re-uploaded with only a JWT (file.controller.ts:24-31) and attached at creation. So "manage a document containing content X in workspace B and mint an editor link on it" is already available: read X (member rw), create a doc in B authored by self, write X in, mint the link — the editor gate at share-link.service.ts:86 passes because the user is the author. The share-link and move gates protect documents the user does not manage; the copy is a distinct new document whose content the user already had full rw access to, and no member-inaccessible state is carried over (comments/share links/analytics are deliberately not copied, document-copy.service.ts:33-37). No permission gate is weakened or bypassed; this only reduces the number of requests, which is a hardening note, not an authorization defect under this lens.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds: no VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN (or equivalent uuid-shape) check exists anywhere on the copy path. document-copy.service.ts:63-64 passes the raw DB `source.fileId` into FileService.copy, and file.service.ts:138-149 interpolates it into `CopySource` via `storageKey(id)` after only deriving the *new* id from safeExtension — the source key is unchecked. Every other DB-fileId->S3 path does validate (document-file.controller.ts:51, api/v1/files.controller.ts:140, document.controller.ts:387 and :428, api/v1/documents.controller.ts:128), and assertFileIdAllowed (document-file-id.util.ts:47-64) only checks extension/type pairing, so it is not a substitute. The sole caller (document.controller.ts:296-308) gates on workspace membership only; DocumentService (document.service.ts:81-102) and PrismaService add no validation. I searched controllers, services, the file module, the Prisma layer and specs for an indirect guard and found no counterexample. Blocking under the security lens, and worse than the reviewer thought: api/v1/documents.controller.ts:79-93 accepts `@Body() body: { title?: string }` as a bare TS type (not a decorated DTO), which the global ValidationPipe in main.ts:66-70 skips, then spreads it straight into prisma update data — a mass-assignment writer that lets a workspace-scoped caller store an arbitrary fileId. That value is unreadable through the validated GET paths, but the copy path duplicates it to a fresh randomUUID()+ext id that passes the pattern, making a foreign/non-servable bucket object downloadable on a document the attacker controls.
